subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equations of the straight lines through the origin that make equal angles with the coordinate axes.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 9, book p.141. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for the angle work that produces 45°, and the second for both equations — the question says lines, plural, so a candidate who writes only y = x has answered half of it. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answer checked: both x − y = 0 and x + y = 0 satisfy the point (0, 0), and each has slope of modulus 1, so each makes 45° with the X-axis and 45° with the Y-axis.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what angle each line makes with the X-axis, and why there are two answers.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the inclination
steps.margin_note: First mark. The two axes are perpendicular, so the angle with the Y-axis is 90° minus the angle with the X-axis. Setting them equal fixes the angle at 45°.
steps.memory_tip: The axes are perpendicular, so the two angles add to 90°. Equal parts of 90° are 45° each.
lines: Let the line make an angle θ with the X-axis.
Then it makes 90° − θ with the Y-axis.
A line at 135° also makes 45° with each axis.

recall.must_convey: That the angle with the Y-axis is 90° − θ, so equal angles give θ = 45°, and 135° works as well.
accept: the angle with the y axis is ninety minus theta
theta equals ninety minus theta so theta is forty five
the inclination is forty five degrees
rendu axes madhya angle equal ante forty five
one thirty five degrees also gives equal angles
reject: the equations are y equals x and y equals minus x

steps.why: A line drawn at 135° leans the other way, but the angle it makes with each axis is still measured as the acute angle, and that angle is again 45°. That is why the question asks for lines and not one line.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 45° and giving only one line.
Taking the angle with the Y-axis as θ as well, which gives no equation.

steps.label: Write the two equations
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A line through the origin has no constant term, so y = mx is enough; only the slope has to be filled in.
steps.memory_tip: Through the origin the constant term is zero, so the line is just y = mx.
lines: A line through the origin is y = mx

recall.must_convey: That the slopes are 1 and −1, and the lines through the origin are y = x and y = −x.
accept: tan forty five is one and tan one thirty five is minus one
the lines are y equals x and y equals minus x
through the origin y equals m x

x minus y is zero and x plus y is zero

steps.why: tan 135° = −tan 45° = −1, so the second line has the same steepness with the opposite lean. Both pass through the origin because the constant term is zero.
common_mistakes: Writing tan 135° as 1 and losing the second line.
Adding a constant term to a line that must pass through the origin.
